title: Math toolkit
description: The `Math` methods that come up constantly in interviews — min/max over arrays, integer rounding modes, and the numerical helpers.

reference.code:
// Min / max over an array — use spread
Math.min(...[3, 1, 4, 1, 5]);    // 1
Math.max(...[3, 1, 4, 1, 5]);    // 5
Math.min();                       // Infinity  (empty)
Math.max();                       // -Infinity (empty)

// Rounding modes
Math.floor(2.9);   //  2
Math.ceil(2.1);    //  3
Math.round(2.5);   //  3   (half rounds toward +Infinity)
Math.round(-2.5);  // -2   (NOT -3)
Math.trunc(2.9);   //  2   (chop fraction, sign-preserving)
Math.trunc(-2.9);  // -2

// Absolute value, sign
Math.abs(-7);      // 7
Math.sign(-3);     // -1   (returns -1, 0, +1)

// Power, roots, logs, hypot
Math.pow(2, 10);   // 1024  (or 2 ** 10)
Math.sqrt(16);     // 4
Math.log2(8);      // 3
Math.hypot(3, 4);  // 5     (sqrt of sum of squares)
notes: `Math.max(arr)` (no spread) returns NaN — `arr` becomes one argument and is coerced to a number.
`Math.round` rounds half toward +Infinity, so `Math.round(-2.5)` is `-2`, not `-3`.
Use `Math.trunc` when you want to discard the fractional part regardless of sign; `Math.floor` rounds toward -Infinity.

questions.q: How do you get the max of an array `arr`?
questions.explain: `Math.max` is variadic — spread the array into its arguments.

questions.q: Which function chops the fractional part without changing sign?

questions.explain: Identity element for max — anything is larger than -Infinity.

exercises.prompt: Find the smallest number in the array.
Compute the Euclidean distance shorthand and round down.

L3.prompt: Given `[12, -7, 3, 25, -1]`, log on separate lines: the sum of absolute values, the min, the max.
hints: Reduce with `Math.abs` for the first line.
